question: If the 6-digit number N09M82 is divisible by 11, then which of the options below can give a possible correct relation between M and N?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility rule of 11: Sum of odd place digits − Sum of even place digits = 0, 11, 22...

(N + 9 + 8) − (0 + M + 2) = 11k

N − M + 15 = 11

N − M = −4 ⇒ M − N = 4

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The 6-digit number N09M82 is divisible by 11.

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd positions and even positions is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of digits at odd places (1st, 3rd, 5th) = N + 9 + 8 = N + 17

⇒ Sum of digits at even places (2nd, 4th, 6th) = 0 + M + 2 = M + 2

⇒ Difference = (N + 17) − (M + 2)

⇒ Difference = N − M + 15

⇒ Equating the difference to 11 to satisfy single-digit constraints (since N and M are digits from 0 to 9):

⇒ N − M + 15 = 11

⇒ N − M = 11 − 15

⇒ N − M = −4

⇒ M − N = 4

**∴ The correct answer is M − N = 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 and 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits are divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 7, 11 and 13 (Block Method)

Form blocks of 3 digits from right to left. If the alternating difference of the sum of these blocks is divisible by 7, 11, or 13, then the number is divisible by that respective divisor.
